paragraphs: Bava ben Buta. Gittin 57a: he acquitted a woman accused of adultery, explaining semen behaves differently over a flame, penetrating the cloth without congealing. Egg white recoils, dries, and congeals. Thus received from his teacher Shammai the elder. A great, elderly sage. Bava Batra 3b: Herod killed the sages, sparing Bava for counsel and blinding him. Repenting, he asked how to repair it. “You extinguished the world’s light, the sages; engage in its light: rebuild the Temple,” for atonement. Mishnah Keritot, end, 25a, mishnah 3: daily he volunteered a suspended guilt-offering, except the day after Yom Kippur, called the pious offering. He swore “by this Dwelling,” the Temple; see Zekharyah ben Hakkatzav. Nedarim 66b: a humble judge making marital peace. A Babylonian married a woman of the Land. He asked two lentils, meaning a little; she took it literally, angering him. “Bring two butzin”—melons; she brought two lamps, butzina in Aramaic. Angry, he said break them on the bava, the door; she thought Bava ben Buta. Sitting judging, he received the blows on his head. “What have you done?” “My husband’s command.” “Daughter, you fulfilled his will. May God give you two sons like Bava ben Buta.” Gilgulei Neshamot [ג״נ]: his spark was in Meir. Devarim Rabbah, Shoftim: a scoffer whose wife heard Meir ordered her to spit in Meir’s face. According to this account, the man and wife in Meir’s story were the couple from Bava’s story in a new incarnation. Meir acted like Bava. The couple were Korach and wife, scoffing at Moses and Aaron. Though Shammai’s student, he followed Beit Hillel on laying hands, Beitzah 20, end of a. The Yerushalmi specifies that he brought three thousand sheep to the Temple Mount. Anyone who wished could bring a burnt offering and lay hands on it. The ruling followed Beit Hillel. See Jerusalem Beitzah 2:4; Chagigah 2:3. In this mystical account, Bava was Jotham reincarnated and was his rectification; see part I, 3721.
